title: Trading bot help
author: G00ber13
selftext: Has anyone here built a successful AI powered stock trading bot? (by successful I mean profitable at the end of the week)  I’ve created one using ChatGPT and had it create a shadow trading system to test different strategies against the real market and when those look promising it paper trades them with Alpaca… my problem is I can’t seem to create a repeatable and profitable strategy with rules. It seems like each week I either damn near break even or take small losses.  I’m looking for insight or recommendations to improve my system.

comments.author: AlgoTradingQuant
comments.body: You need to backtest strategies and find one(s) that have an edge before attempting to automate it.

comments.author: mehatebananas
comments.body: Forward testing only tells you what impact realistic executions are going to have on a strategy. It doesn't tell you if a strategy has real edge. Backtest at least 5 years of data before wasting your time and money trying to deploy something.

comments.author: Maleficent-Success-6
comments.body:
Does each strategy get frozen before it moves from shadow testing to Alpaca paper trading, or does ChatGPT keep tweaking it?

If the rules are still changing during the test, it's hard to tell whether you're validating a strategy or constantly starting a new experiment.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: I haven't built one, and I'd drop "profitable at the end of the week" as the test, since a week has too few trades to separate an edge from luck, and results near break-even are what most simple rules give once costs are counted. What I'd do is set a fixed number of trades per strategy before judging it, compare each one against holding the index or random entries over the same days, and keep the rules frozen while it runs. With a shadow system testing many strategies, some will look promising by chance, so count every strategy tried and ask for a bigger result as the count grows. Cymetica's Backtest Labs is one place to test a rule against history with fees included.

comments.author: Sea-Air-1781
comments.body: So I am about two months in of a lot of work and I still can’t really say it’s profitable. I’ve been back testing a new system with one clerk that is doing bull or bear put spreads on the XSP depending on morning signals from indicators like $tick and volume along with some candle reading. So far and back testing it looks really good and I started last week once again. It’s just like we trade. It just is better at not being emotional. The easy part is to get into a trade and the hard part is to cut it. I have put hard rules on cutting the trade and even though I’m back testing at 58% the amount with the win versus loss is where I’m hoping I can start making some money. I’ve tried every other possibility that I can think of that fits a bot, I had nine different bots running different strategies and they would make money and then lose it all.

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body:
A profitable week is too short a promotion rule, especially when the shadow system tries many candidates. Freeze each candidate before paper trading, count every failed variant, and compare its after-cost result with a simple baseline over the same untouched period. Keep execution failures separate from strategy losses; changing both at once makes the diagnosis harder.
